short: Skin-closed ECoG implant used at home without investigators (M13): standard, one user, skin-closed link predates it; 89% spelling accuracy pools inactive steps and has no chance level.
position: The paper [@vansteensel2016] changes the device and its operation (M13): subdural ECoG with a subcutaneous transmitter, nothing through the skin, used at home without investigators from day 197. Both departures are standard: the skin-closed link predates it [@guenther2009], and independent home use rests on one participant, though none of the 19 independent-use pattern matches predates it. The claim that one locked-in user can communicate without the team holds, and the [later] 7-year follow-up of the same user confirms durability, not generality [@vansteensel2024]. The 89% spelling accuracy pools target and more numerous non-target steps with no chance level or false-click rate (M12), and two letters per minute with unspecified word prediction is far below [later] intracortical typing [@jude2026].
